detail.overview:
Overview

New to crypto, machine learning or Kaggle? No background needed — skip straight to the
AI-assisted start
tab: your Kaggle key, the competition link, one prompt, and a first result in five minutes.
Come back here when you want to know why it worked.

The whole competition in ten lines

1. You submit a notebook, not predictions: it trains inside the run, on CPU, without internet.
2. Every day the bot retrains it on the history before the test day (the last 30 days in train.csv, plus the archive if you use it) and scores it on one new day — real PnL, not AUC.
3. submission.csv holds one number per token: the sell target tp, or 0 for *do not buy*.
4. The Kaggle leaderboard is a sandbox on one day; the standings that matter are the bot's, on this tab.
5. The competition closes on 30 November 2026, 23:59 UTC. That is the freeze: your last version is locked.
6. Then 14 days of scoring on days that did not exist at the freeze — 1–14 December.
7. The official score is the sum of those 14 daily PnLs. Skipping everything scores exactly zero.
8. To be eligible for prizes, send your notebook to the bot — @pumpfun_competition_bot — at least once and link your Kaggle account (/link) before the freeze; unlinked entries are scored under an anonymous code. Scoring through the bot is also 3–4× faster than on Kaggle: your notebook runs on dedicated hardware and the trial score comes straight back to the chat. The bot is also your direct line to the organisers: we see everything you write there and answer right in that chat — questions, errors, ideas, we are there to help.
9. Prizes for ten places plus community awards; a public review of the winning notebooks comes before payment.
10. The exact numbers live in "How this competition is built" further down; the rules are on the Rules tab.

First: join the chat

Most of what you will want to ask is faster to ask than to look up.

👉 t.me/BlockchainExploratorsChat

That is where the organisers and participants sit. Several people there work with Solana and
on-chain data professionally, so questions about the domain itself — how launches behave, what a
bundle really means, why a pool ends up empty — get answered properly rather than guessed at.
Questions about the competition mechanics get answered there too, usually within minutes.

The submission bot is the same story in private: that one chat is both where you upload your
notebook and your direct line to the whole organising team. Everything you write there is read by
the organisers, and the answer comes back from a person, not from a model. You are not going to be
left alone with an error message you cannot parse.

Open solutions from the league

Three participants have opened the notebooks that earned their league results, with a digest of
the approach and the author's own comment. The posts live in the chat; the notebooks are public in
the Code tab of this competition. This is the fastest way to see what actually works on this data.…
detail.evaluation:
Evaluation

Your score is total simulated trading PnL — the sum over every token in the test set. Not an average, not an accuracy: the number is what the strategy would have earned.

Payoff per token

Let tp be your submitted level for a token.

If tp = 0 (skip):

pnl = 0

If 3 <= tp <= 100 (buy with that take-profit):

pnl = tp - 1 - 0.3 if the token reached tp within the hour
pnl = max(final_x - 1 - 0.3, -1) otherwise

Where:

- 0.3 is the trading cost (fees plus slippage), charged on every position you take
- final_x is the price of the last trade of the hour divided by your entry price
- the -1 floor means you cannot lose more than the position

Score = sum of pnl over all test tokens. Higher is better.

Entry, and what "reached" means

- Entry price is the price of the last trade at or before migration + 60 seconds. This is your fill; you do not choose it.
- The evaluation window is the next 60 minutes after that snapshot.
- A token reached level tp if its *sustained* maximum within the window is at least tp.

"Sustained" is important. The maximum is computed after discarding the top max(1%, 1) highest-priced trades of the window. A single printed trade at an absurd price therefore cannot create a level you get paid at — because in reality you could not have sold into it. If a token has too few trades for that trim to be meaningful, no level is considered reachable and the position is carried to the end of the hour.

Worked examples

A token whose sustained maximum is 10x and which ends the hour at 0.5x:
your tp | what happens | pnl0 | skipped | 0.00
5 | take-profit fires at 5x | +3.70
10 | fires exactly at the top | +8.70
20 | never fires, held to end of hour | -0.80
The same token, four different opinions, four very different outcomes.…
detail.data_or_tools:
Data

The raw trade tape, not engineered features. Everything the chain knew about a token up to your decision moment — and nothing after it.

Coverage: the tape starts on 2026-08-21 and only grows — every daily update adds the newest day and never removes an old one, so a notebook written against an earlier version keeps finding every file it read. The labelled window inside it slides: the last 30 full days are training, the day after them is the test day — roughly 16,000 train tokens and about 600 test tokens, depending on how busy the market was. The last two hours before the test day are excluded from training — that gap is built into train.csv, nothing for you to do. Both files move forward by one day with every daily update. The tape older than the train window is there for history features — wallet or creator behaviour that needs to look back further than the label window — and its answers are in train_archive.csv, for validation on old days. Several GB in total and growing by roughly 0.2 GB a day; a token lives in the partition of its migration day, so you can read exactly the days you need.
